question: An image is formed at a distance of 30 cm from a convex mirror when the object is placed 40 cm from the mirror. The magnification produced by the mirror will be _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**+3/4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Magnification (m)** produced by a spherical mirror is the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object, which is also related to the **object distance (u)** and **image distance (v)**.
 
• According to the **New Cartesian Sign Convention**, the **object distance (u)** is always taken as **negative** because the object is placed in front of the mirror. In this case, **u = -40 cm**.
 
• For a **convex mirror**, the image is always **virtual, erect, and formed behind the mirror**. Therefore, the **image distance (v)** is taken as **positive**. In this case, **v = +30 cm**.
 
• The formula for magnification (m) for a mirror is given by **m = -v / u**. Substituting the given values into the formula: **m = -(30) / (-40)**.
